rows.description: A preschooler stands tall with chest out after a success or hides behind a leg when shy. Posture shows pride, boldness or wariness; a child who shrinks may need gentle warm-up time rather than pressure to perform.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler spins, dances or claps for joy at music, a birthday or a win. Movement shows delight and helps regulate energy; joining in strengthens bonding more than praising or correcting.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child turns away or walks off after a rebuke, a refusal or a lost game. It can mean upset, embarrassment or a wish for space; a calm invitation to return works better than following with demands.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler covers eyes at a scary scene or ears at a loud siren. It is an early self-protection strategy and a sign the input is too much; respecting it and offering a quieter space teaches that limits are allowed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child pulls back, ducks or stiffens when someone hugs or touches them against their wish. This is a valid signal of discomfort; caring adults respect it, and the child can practise saying no and telling a trusted adult if pressure continues.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, admiration, trust

rows.subtype: Covering the mouth when shy or surprised [Expressing]
rows.description: A child puts a hand over the mouth after a slip, in giggles or in shy surprise. It may signal embarrassment, mischief or awe; context tells which, and a gentle smile helps a child feel safe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, embarrassment, shyness, surprise

rows.description: A preschooler chews a nail, picks at clothes or fidgets when waiting or nervous. These actions are self-soothing, not naughtiness; teaching a fidget toy or deep breaths works better than punishment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, relief from stress

rows.description: A preschooler learns that hugging or kissing is a choice, with a right to say no, even to relatives. Adults who accept a wave or high-five instead teach the child that their body belongs to them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child learns that safe touch feels comfortable and unsafe touch feels confusing or scary, and that private body areas are not for others to touch. If touch feels wrong or someone asks for secrecy, the child should tell a trusted adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child learns that arm's length is a fair distance for many talks and that some people, like family, may stand closer. Children who crowd others or freeze when crowded may need gentle coaching and clear words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
